title: Understanding my metrics
intro: Every concept and abbreviation used in Sporty, with guidelines to read them.

ctl.name: CTL — Fitness (Chronic Training Load)
ctl.short: Your daily training load averaged over ~42 days, weighted towards recent days. It reflects your long-term training level.
ctl.read: The higher it goes, the more volume you can absorb. A steady rise of 3–5 points per week is sustainable.

atl.name: ATL — Fatigue (Acute Training Load)
atl.short: Same calculation as CTL but over ~7 days: your recent fatigue.
atl.read: It reacts quickly: after a hard block it rises above CTL, then drops within a few rest days.

tsb.name: TSB — Form (Training Stress Balance)
tsb.short: CTL − ATL: long-term fitness minus recent fatigue.
tsb.read: Negative (−10 to −30): loading phase, normal in training. Around 0 to +15: fresh, ideal for racing. Below −30: overreaching risk.

tss.name: TSS — Training Stress Score
tss.short: Session load combining duration and intensity. 100 TSS ≈ one hour at threshold.
tss.read: Sporty computes it, from most to least reliable, from pace (running: rTSS; swimming: sTSS), heart-rate curve (TRIMP) or perceived effort (RPE).

rtss.name: rTSS — Running TSS
rtss.short: TSS computed from your pace relative to your threshold pace (derived from VDOT).
rtss.read: Used for running when your VDOT is known.

stss.name: sTSS — Swimming TSS
stss.short: TSS computed from your swim pace relative to your CSS: intensity³ × duration × 100.
stss.read: More reliable than heart rate in the water, where wrist HR is often inaccurate. Requires your CSS in your profile.

trimp.name: TRIMP — Training Impulse
trimp.short: Load computed from time spent at each heart-rate level, weighting high heart rates heavily.
trimp.read: An easy one-hour run gives ~50–80, a hard session much more. Comparable across your sessions, not between people.

vdot.name: VDOT — Running performance index
vdot.short: Jack Daniels' index derived from your performances: it sums up your level and drives your training paces and race predictions.
vdot.read: Each VDOT point ≈ 1–2% faster. 40 = regular recreational runner, 50 = good club level, 60+ = very strong.

vo2max.name: VO2max
vo2max.short: Maximal oxygen uptake (ml/kg/min) estimated by your watch.
vo2max.read: Similar in spirit to VDOT but computed differently by each brand: compare it mostly to itself over time.

maxHr.name: Max HR
maxHr.short: The highest heart rate you can reach. It anchors your heart-rate zones.
maxHr.read: Formulas (220 − age) are rough: a value measured at the end of a maximal effort is far more accurate.

restingHr.name: Resting HR
restingHr.short: Heart rate on waking, at rest.
restingHr.read: It drops as fitness improves. A rise of more than 5 bpm above your normal often signals fatigue, stress or illness.

lthr.name: LTHR — Lactate threshold heart rate
lthr.short: Heart rate you can sustain for about an hour of hard effort (≈ average HR over the last 20 minutes of a 30-minute test).
lthr.read: The most reliable anchor for personalised heart-rate zones.

karvonen.name: Karvonen method
karvonen.short: Zones computed from heart-rate reserve (max HR − resting HR) rather than max HR alone.
karvonen.read: More personal than plain % of max HR, since it accounts for your resting HR.

hrZones.name: Heart-rate zones Z1–Z5
hrZones.short: Five intensity ranges based on your HR: Z1 recovery, Z2 endurance, Z3 tempo, Z4 threshold, Z5 VO2max.
hrZones.read: Classic guideline: about 80% of time in Z1–Z2, the rest in Z4–Z5, little Z3 ("polarised" distribution).

hrv.name: HRV — Heart-rate variability
hrv.short: Variation in time between heartbeats, measured overnight (ms). It reflects the balance of your nervous system.
hrv.read: Only compare it to your own baseline: several days below it means incomplete recovery.

spo2.name: SpO2
spo2.read: Normally 95–100%. An unusual drop can signal altitude, illness or night-time breathing issues.

acwr.name: ACWR — Acute:chronic workload ratio
acwr.short: Load over the last 7 days divided by average load over the last 4 weeks.
acwr.read: 0.8–1.3: safe zone. Above 1.5: too sharp an increase, higher injury risk.

monotony.name: Monotony
monotony.short: Average daily load of the week divided by its day-to-day variability.
monotony.read: Above 2: the week is too uniform (not enough easy days), a driver of overtraining.

strain.name: Strain
strain.read: High strain combines big volume with little variety: most illnesses and injuries happen in such weeks.

decoupling.name: Aerobic decoupling
decoupling.short: Drift of the pace-to-HR ratio between the first and second half of a long run.
decoupling.read: Under 5%: solid aerobic base. Above, HR rises at constant pace: endurance needs work.

cardiacDrift.name: Cardiac drift
cardiacDrift.short: Rise in HR during a session while effort stays the same.
cardiacDrift.read: Low (< 5%) on an easy run = good adaptation. Heat and dehydration increase it.

ef.name: EF — Efficiency Factor
ef.short: Speed divided by HR on easy runs.
ef.read: If it rises, you go faster for the same cardiac effort: the best sign of aerobic progress.

gap.name: GAP — Grade-adjusted pace
gap.short: Equivalent flat-ground pace, correcting for uphills and downhills.
gap.read: Lets you compare a hilly run with a flat one.

rpe.name: RPE — Rate of perceived exertion
rpe.short: How hard a session felt (1–5 scale in Sporty).
rpe.read: Used to estimate load when there is no usable heart rate.

readiness.name: Readiness
readiness.short: Summary of your HRV, resting HR, sleep and form (TSB) compared to your baseline.
readiness.read: Low: prefer an easy session or rest. Good: green light for a hard session.

css.name: CSS — Critical swim speed
css.short: The pace you can hold for about 30 minutes: your swimming "threshold". Computed from an all-out 400 m and 200 m: (400 − 200) / (T400 − T200).
css.read: Reference for swim training paces and for sTSS. Expressed in min/100 m.

swolf.name: SWOLF
swolf.short: Time (seconds) + number of strokes for one pool length.
swolf.read: Lower is more efficient. Only compare values from pools of the same length.

swimPace.name: Swim pace (/100 m)
swimPace.read: The standard swimming unit: 2'00/100m = 1,500 m in 30 minutes.
